items.title: llm 0.37
items.snippet: Release: llm 0.37 There's a lot of stuff in this new release of my LLM CLI tool and Python library, representing around two months of accumulated features and fixes. I added gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6.1-terra , plus a new llm openai endpoint add command to make it easier to configure additional models that use OpenAI-compatible endpoints. I switched the default model (if you have not set your own default) to gpt-6-luna - half the price of the previous default, gpt-5.6-luna . LLM's support for embeddi
items.title_ar: إصدار llm 0.37 يضيف نماذج OpenAI جديدة وأمر إعداد endpoint
items.summary_ar: أصدر Simon Willison الإصدار 0.37 من أداة CLI ومكتبة Python الخاصة بـ LLM، ويجمع ميزات وإصلاحات تراكمت خلال شهرين. أضاف الإصدار نموذجي gpt-6.1-sol و gpt-6.1-terra، وأمر llm openai endpoint add لإعداد نماذج إضافية متوافقة مع OpenAI-compatible endpoints. كما غيّر النموذج الافتراضي إلى gpt-6-luna بنصف سعر النموذج السابق.
items.why_ar: أداة شائعة لتجربة الموديلات بسرعة، وأمر الإضافة يسهّل ربط نماذج داخلية متوافقة مع OpenAI في أي POC.
items.title_en: llm 0.37 adds new OpenAI models and an endpoint setup command
items.summary_en: Simon Willison released llm 0.37, a CLI tool and Python library for LLMs, bundling about two months of features and fixes. It adds gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6.1-terra models and an llm openai endpoint add command for OpenAI-compatible endpoints. The default model switched to gpt-6-luna, which costs half the previous default.
items.why_en: It is a widely used tool for quickly testing models, and the endpoint command makes it easier to wire in internal OpenAI-compatible models for a POC.

items.title: Anthropic warns that it’s very close to RSI capability, aka self-building AI
items.snippet: RSI is the point at which AI grows so good at training itself that it spawns a dramatic acceleration of AI capabilities. To the AI doomers, RSI represents the cataclysm from which there is no return.
items.title_ar: Anthropic تحذر من قرب الوصول إلى قدرة RSI
items.summary_ar: حذّرت Anthropic من أنها أصبحت قريبة جداً من قدرة RSI، أي AI قادرة على بناء نفسها. يصف النص RSI بأنها النقطة التي تصبح فيها AI بارعة في تدريب نفسها، فتتسارع قدراتها بشكل كبير.
items.why_ar: موضوع مهم لأبحاث سلامة الموديلات وقدرات التحسين الذاتي، ويصلح لورقة تحليلية.
items.title_en: Anthropic warns it is very close to RSI capability
items.summary_en: Anthropic warned it is very close to RSI capability, meaning self-building AI. The article describes RSI as the point where AI becomes so good at training itself that its capabilities accelerate dramatically.
items.why_en: This topic is important for research on model safety and self-improvement capabilities and could support an analytical paper.

items.title: ctoldigital/axuse
items.snippet: Accessibility-first browser & computer use for AI agents — one MCP server for every harness (Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Antigravity). Instruments the DOM/accessibility tree via CDP instead of screenshot loops: diffed snapshots, stable element refs, trusted input, typed errors. Zero dependencies
items.title_ar: أداة accessibility-first لتشغيل المتصفح والحاسوب عبر MCP واحد لوكلاء AI
items.summary_ar: يقدم المشروع MCP server واحداً يعمل مع عدة harnesses مثل Codex و Claude Code و OpenCode و Antigravity. يعتمد على قراءة DOM وaccessibility tree عبر CDP بدلاً من حلقات screenshot، مع diffed snapshots وstable element refs وtrusted input وtyped errors. ويوصف بأنه بلا dependencies.
items.why_ar: يفيد أي agent يحتاج تفاعلاً موثوقاً مع الواجهات بتكلفة أقل من تحليل الصور المتكرر.
items.title_en: Accessibility-first browser and computer use through one MCP server
items.summary_en: The project provides a single MCP server that works across several harnesses such as Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and Antigravity. It reads the DOM and accessibility tree via CDP instead of screenshot loops, using diffed snapshots, stable element refs, trusted input, and typed errors. It is described as having zero dependencies.
items.why_en: It offers a more reliable way for agents to interact with interfaces than repeated screenshot analysis.

items.title: Goldman bans traders and bankers from using AI coding tools
items.snippet: Goldman Sachs has banned traders and other employees from using advanced AI tools for coding over productivity and risk concerns, according to Bloomberg
items.title_ar: Goldman Sachs يمنع المتداولين والمصرفيين من أدوات AI للبرمجة
items.summary_ar: أفادت Bloomberg بأن Goldman Sachs منع المتداولين وموظفين آخرين من استخدام أدوات AI متقدمة للبرمجة. يرجع القرار إلى مخاوف تتعلق بالإنتاجية والمخاطر.
items.why_ar: يوضح قيود الحوكمة التي قد تواجه أي POC للبرمجة بالذكاء الاصطناعي داخل بنك.
items.title_en: Goldman Sachs bans traders and bankers from AI coding tools
items.summary_en: Bloomberg reports that Goldman Sachs has banned traders and other employees from using advanced AI tools for coding. The decision is linked to productivity and risk concerns.
items.why_en: It shows the governance limits that any AI coding POC inside a bank will need to address.

items.title: السعودية تنتقل من بناء القدرة الحاسوبية إلى تشغيل الذكاء الاصطناعي على نطاق واسع - الشرق الأوسط

items.summary_ar: تتجه السعودية من بناء البنية الحاسوبية إلى مرحلة تشغيل AI على نطاق واسع. يشير الخبر إلى تحول في الأولويات دون تفاصيل عن المنصات أو الشراكات.
items.why_ar: يهم المهندس لأن الانتقال إلى التشغيل واسع النطاق يرفع الطلب على ممارسات inference وتحسين استهلاك GPU داخل البنك.
items.title_en: Saudi Arabia shifts from building compute capacity to running AI at scale
items.summary_en: Saudi Arabia is moving from building computing infrastructure to operating AI at large scale. The report signals a shift in priorities but gives no details on platforms or partnerships.
items.why_en: This matters because large-scale operation raises the importance of inference efficiency and GPU optimization practices for a bank's AI workloads.

items.title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents
items.snippet: Robot agents built on vision-language models depend on both the planner and its harness: the tools, feedback, memory, and recovery logic around it. We first freeze an open-weight teacher and improve its harness through recursive self-improvement (RSI): frontier LLM agents read the teacher's trajectories and propose harness edits, and each edit is accepted only if it passes a paired statistical test. items.title: From Fragmentation to Fusion: A Survey and Roadmap for Omnimodal Embeddings
items.snippet: Embedding models underpin virtually every modern AI system, from search engines to recommendation systems. Despite shared mathematical foundations, research on embedding models remains fragmented by modality: the communities develop largely in isolation, seldom exchanging insights. We argue that this fragmentation obscures a deeper convergence. Driven by contrastive learning, Transformer architectures, and a granularity shift, embedding research across modalities is converging toward a common set of principles, even as modality-specific challenges remain underexplored. To reason across this convergence without conflating it, we propose a framework of three progressively harder capabilities:

items.title: Self-Improvement with Auxiliary Rewards: Learning from Verified Traces and Evaluating Transfer
items.snippet: Answer-level rewards cannot distinguish reasoning traces with equally correct outcomes. We study whether auxiliary trajectory preferences improve small-language-model self-improvement and transfer under limited supervision. We compare confidence-based (SC) and entropy-based metrics (UID-Conj.), which combines global entropy variation and local smoothness, through online reward augmentation and offline training on correct responses. Online experiments adapt Qwen3-1.7B on 30 AIME problems without reference answers; offline experiments use historical AIME problems. UID-Conj. improves the online macro-average across the adaptation benchmark and three transfer benchmarks by 2.08 percentage points

items.title: DecisionRank: On-Policy Distillation for Decision-Model Rerankers
items.snippet: Decision models target structured tasks by directly predicting choices or scores, avoiding autoregressive decoding latency. However, transferring a generative LLM's ranking knowledge to a decision model remains challenging: the teacher expresses preferences through a ranked list of document ID sequences, while the student determines the ranking using scores from the first-token position. To bridge this gap, we introduce DecisionRank, a decision model trained through item-space on-policy distillation (OPD). items.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
items.snippet: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. We study their intersection through the agent harness: an executable runtime that constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and manages budgets around video models. items.title: Diagnosing the Reference Gap: What Visual Scaffolds Can and Cannot Fix in Multimodal Reasoning
items.snippet: Multimodal large language models can recognize visual content yet struggle to reason reliably over it across multiple steps. In counting, a model may see all objects but lose track of which ones it has counted. We argue that such failures, commonly attributed to perception, reveal a reference gap: the failure to bind language to the relevant visual entities, regions, or locations. Motivated by the theory of visual routines, we test whether external references such as numbering can narrow this gap. items.title: MAServeBench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent LLM Serving Systems with Hierarchical Collaboration Workloads
items.snippet: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) coordinate specialized agents to solve complex tasks, turning each user request into interdependent model and tool operations. Unlike independent requests, these operations become ready at different times and consume evolving context as agents coordinate and exchange results. This creates changing patterns of concurrency, computation, and memory demand that can expose different bottlenecks in LLM serving hardware. Yet benchmarking these effects requires capturing the collaboration rules that generate serving workloads, beyond the requests observed during execution. items.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Teacher Evolution
items.snippet: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), which aligns a student model's token-level distribution with that of its self-teacher prompted by privileged context, has emerged as a promising direction to mitigate reward sparsity in sequence-level post-training paradigms. However, OPSD often fails to achieve continuous performance gains during training. In this paper, we find that the model's limited self-teaching capability underlies this phenomenon by generating unreliable guidance on certain samples. items.title_ar: Deepscient: منصة تجمع AI والباحثين البشر لحل مسائل علمية صعبة
items.summary_ar: يقدم المشروع إطاراً يجمع AI مع البشر لمعالجة مشكلات علمية معقدة، ويتكون من 12 مرحلة و55 مقرراً. يضم 36 tool و98 skill مع تركيز على evidence chain وقابلية إعادة الإنتاج reproducibility. النص المتاح قصير ولا يوضح نتائج تجريبية.
items.why_ar: يقدم نموذجاً لبناء agents علمية تحتاج تتبعاً للأدلة وقابلية للتكرار، وهو مناسب لموضوعات بحثية.
items.title_en: Deepscient: combining AI and human researchers on hard scientific problems
items.summary_en: The project presents a framework that pairs AI with humans to tackle complex scientific problems, with 12 stages and 55 courses. It includes 36 tools and 98 skills, with a focus on evidence chains and reproducibility. The available text is brief and does not report experimental results.
items.why_en: It is a useful reference for building scientific agents that need traceable evidence and repeatable runs, which suits a research paper topic.
